meta.title: Genome Viewer — what the DNA that makes no protein does
meta.description: The non-coding genome explained for an eight-year-old and for a postdoc, with real molecular structures from the Protein Data Bank and a viewer of AlphaGenome predictions.
meta.ogAlt: A violet and amber point cloud on black: the atoms of a real structure from the Protein Data Bank.
brand.name: Genome Viewer
hero.title: Almost all of your DNA makes no protein. Here is what it does.
hero.lead: Every point on this screen is an atom whose position was measured in a lab. When it trembles, it trembles because that is how it was measured.
structure.5XJC: human spliceosome just before exon ligation

chapter.label: Chapter
scale.title: From two nanometers to two meters
scale.lead: Scroll slowly. The structures appear at their true relative size, taken from their own coordinates.
refs.title: References
refs.lead: Every number on this page carries its source. Structures cite the primary publication of their PDB entry.
foot.real: What is real: the position of every atom and its thermal motion (B-factor) are measurements from the Protein Data Bank, CC0 data. What is not: the transitions from one molecule to the next are a visual device, not a biological process. No physics is computed here: positions and motion arrive already measured.
foot.data: The viewer's predictions come from AlphaGenome (Google DeepMind). This site is unofficial.
